text:
Lithium brine has been found at the Hadrow Flats survey site, according to preliminary assay results released on 14 March 2031.

Brine samples drawn from 18 test wells averaged 412 milligrams of lithium per litre, the Hadrow Flats Survey Consortium reported. The figures appear in the Hadrow Flats Preliminary Assay Report (Report No. HFS-31-07), which was presented at the Consortium's public briefing in Tollamere.

Dr. Perrin Valkoski, lead field geochemist for the Consortium, said the results confirm that the brine is present across the area tested.

"The consistency across all 18 wells is what stands out," Valkoski said. "These samples show lithium in the brine at a meaningful concentration, and that is the finding the team set out to test."

The report is described as preliminary. Further analysis will be needed before the Consortium can say how much of the resource lies beneath the flats.
